preamble: In Sotho-Tswana, root-initial /r/ hardens to the aspirated stop [tʰ] in post-nasal contexts, part of a broader post-nasal fortition that also turns /l/ into [t], /f/ into [pʰ] and /s/ into [tsʰ]. In Setswana the change is triggered by the reflexive prefix, the 1st person singular object marker and the class 9 noun prefix, all of which historically contained a homorganic nasal; the nasal itself is often lost while its effect remains. Acoustic VOT values of the derived [tʰ] match underlying /tʰ/, so the shift is categorical. Coetzee (2000), citing Poulos & Louwrens (1994), reports the same N + r > (n)th pattern in Northern Sotho.

examples.note: The reflexive prefix /i(N)-/ surfaces as [i-] but still triggers hardening of root-initial /r/ to [tʰ].

sources: Bennett, W. G., Diemer, M., Kerford, J., Probert, T., & Wesi, T. (2016). Setswana (South African). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 46(2), 235-246. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100316000050

Coetzee, A. W. (2000). Post nasal neutralization phenomena in Tswana. University of Massachusetts. https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/coetzee/wp-content/uploads/sites/177/2014/10/Tswana-post-nasal-devoicing.pdf
